manifest.title: Buzz
manifest.author: Marcus Quinn <marcus@marcusquinn.com>
manifest.description: Self-hosted, channel-driven workspace where humans and AI agents collaborate with shared context, portable Nostr identities, ACP-compatible runtimes, Git hosting, search, and automation.
manifest.tagline: Shared workspace for humans and AI agents
manifest.postInstallMessage:
Buzz is running as a private relay and Git forge.

First-owner setup:
1. Open the Buzz desktop or mobile client and create or import an identity. Back up the private nsec securely; never paste it into Cloudron.
2. Choose **Join a community**. Do not choose **Create a community** or **I own the community**; in Buzz v0.4.22 those options use the hosted Builderlab workflow.
3. Enter `wss://$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN` and copy the identity's public npub.
4. In the Cloudron Web Terminal, run `/app/code/buzz-ctl set-owner <NPUB_OR_HEX_PUBKEY>`.
5. Return to Buzz and select **Connect** or **Retry**.

Verify with `/app/code/buzz-ctl owner`, `/app/code/buzz-ctl list-members`, and `/app/code/buzz-ctl status`.

The app URL intentionally serves public NIP-11 metadata and a static invite/Git-forge shell. Team data remains protected by signed Buzz protocol authentication and relay membership. Do not add .htaccess or blanket HTTP Basic Auth; it can break supported clients and health checks.

External push delivery and the deployment-admin host are disabled by default.
manifest.changelog:
* Add Cloudron community catalog metadata and publishing runbook.
* Add a privacy-reviewed 3:1 screenshot hero.
